findings.summary: The TOO LOOSE sentence still names a trigger that does not fire, one sentence before the row's own correction of it. It reads 'git renders a MOVED committed line as delete+add, so sorting the file or INSERTING AN ENTRY ABOVE an already-argued rounds:<task> line re-arms the escape for a later commit', and the next arrow says 'A draft of this row said the trigger was "inserting one reviewer: entry above it", which does NOT fire on its own ... The line has to MOVE.' Measured in a scratch repo seeded with HEAD's real baselines/review.txt plus a rounds:M4.21 line: inserting 'reviewer:R9<TAB>not a defect, measured' immediately above it renders the rounds: line as CONTEXT and the shipped awk block does not match (cap still refuses); relocating the rounds: line to the top renders delete+add and the awk DOES match (cap argued). So the false half of the recipe was corrected in the disclosure and left standing in the claim.
findings.failure_scenario: Whoever implements M4.31 builds the too-loose regression test from the first sentence -- stage an insertion above a committed rounds: line -- observes the gate correctly refuse, and concludes the too-loose arm is unreachable. The staged-vs-HEAD primitive then ships with no test for the RELOCATION case, which is the one arm actually measured, leaving the exact bypass M4.31 was filed to close unpinned. This is the wrong-worked-example defect the M4.26 row records twice about itself (`git show :`, `NF > 1`), and it is the round-6 shape: the correction moved the error instead of removing it. Fix: drop 'or inserting an entry above' and say 'a staged edit that RELOCATES the line (sorting the file, for example)'.

findings.summary: Two new factual claims that the tree contradicts, neither present in HEAD (grepped: 'two rows below' and 'third recurrence' both absent from HEAD's backlog). (a) 'two rows below M4.12's own "NO COUNT HERE, deliberately"' -- in the staged file M4.12 is line 265 and M4.21 is line 268, with M4.19 (266) and M4.20 (267) between them, so it is THREE rows below. It is also a positional citation into a file this same commit inserts eight rows into (M4.26-M4.34), i.e. the 'citation with a half-life' the M4.26 row denounces in this same diff, and the same class this round DELETED from M4.30 ('four lines above', actually 15). (b) 'the third recurrence in this milestone' -- M4.19's already-landed body (2953b5a) says 'THIS IS THE THIRD TIME A COUNT IN PROSE HAS GONE STALE in this milestone' about its own 178/180/181 test counts, and M4.12's row (line 265) documents its own six->nine->twelve. M4.21's is therefore at least the fourth, and the tree now carries two incompatible ordinals for one phenomenon -- with none of the 'neither is reconstructible, so the split is recorded rather than settled' disclosure this same diff makes for the 8-vs-7 split.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader following the pointer lands on the M4.20 row and cannot find the 'NO COUNT HERE' sentence, so the cross-reference that was added to make the pattern visible instead costs a search. A reader tallying the recurrences reads 'third' in M4.19's body and 'third' in the M4.21 row for two different events and cannot use the ordinal to tell whether the pattern is still growing, which is its only purpose. Both claims go stale again the moment another row is filed between lines 265 and 268, which M4.26 and M4.31 make likely. Fix: name the row ('M4.12's own NO COUNT HERE, deliberately') with no distance, and either drop the ordinal or state it as a floor with its two conflicting sources named, exactly as the 8-vs-7 paragraph does.

findings.summary: The load-bearing NINE counts DISCLOSURES, not skips, and the row's claim about M4.12 is false. The M4.21 row states 'M4.12 hit the cap at 12 rounds with both reviewers passing and zero majors, the argument was written into baselines/review.txt as the message directs, and the gate still refused; the commit landed with SKIP=check-reviewed STATED IN ITS BODY instead.' Measured: `git log -1 --format=%B 67606ab` contains no 'SKIP', no 'check-reviewed' and no 'reviewed' at all, and its Gates paragraph lists eleven gates while omitting check-reviewed entirely; `git log --grep=SKIP=check-reviewed` returns nine commits and M4.12 is not among them. Yet M4.12 demonstrably bypassed the gate: all twelve of its verdict files were written 18:02-21:49 on 2026-09-04 and the commit is 22:16 +1000, so ROUNDS was 12 at commit time and the cap would have refused. The checkable halves hold -- 12 distinct hashes, final hash c5cf7043208b with reviewer=pass and test-reviewer=pass and zero blocking/major. Consequence for the newly written text: 'NINE commits in M4 landed that way -- measured with git log --grep=SKIP=check-reviewed, not counted from memory' (gate comment), '**nine** commits landed that way' (review.md) and 'NINE commits in M4 landed that way' (test javadoc) all measure body disclosures, and this repository holds a counter-example proving the grep undercounts actual skips. The direction favours the change's own argument, so nothing is weakened -- but a floor is presented as a measurement, and the row asserts a body statement that is not there.
findings.failure_scenario: A future reader auditing the escape's justification greps for the nine, finds M4.12 absent while the same row says M4.12 landed with the skip stated in its body, and cannot tell which claim is wrong -- the 'measured, not remembered' assurance is what makes the discrepancy corrosive rather than harmless, since it invites trusting the number without re-measuring. The same reader looking for M4.12's disclosure finds none, so the row's central FOUND BY FOLLOWING THE INSTRUCTION evidence is unreproducible from the tree. Fix costs two words plus one clause: 'AT LEAST nine' at all three sites, and the M4.12 sentence rewritten to what the tree shows -- the gate refused and the commit landed with no disclosure at all, which is a stronger argument for the escape and also an instance of M0.48's rule that a skipped review must be stated in the body.

findings.summary: The reason given for deleting the running total is true only of the tree BEFORE this edit. 12b now says 'no running total is kept here, because two places in the tree already carry different ones'. After this diff exactly one place carries a total: backlog M0.21, 'review.md rule 12b was broken five times in one session'. Grepped the standards, the staged backlog, the skills and scripts for a second total ('12b', 'index moved', 'lost', 'five times', 'four times', 'three times') and there is none -- the second of the two differing totals was 12b's own 'Three were lost ... A fourth was lost', which this diff removes.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader who accepts the justification goes looking for the two conflicting totals in order to reconcile them, finds one, and the sentence reads as exactly the unchecked claim about the tree that this paragraph was rewritten to stop making. Fix: 'because the tree already carries one (M0.21: five times) and a counter incremented by hand goes stale.'

findings.summary: 'roughly a quarter of the verdict files carry no task at all' is a proportion of a moving population, quoted two sentences after the paragraph refuses to quote a denominator for precisely that reason. Measured at review time: 90 of 407 verdict files carry no task, 22.1% -- nearer a fifth than a quarter, and the denominator grows on every recorded verdict, including the two this round adds. The objection the preceding sentence makes ('it counts reviewed TASKS and tasks keep being reviewed ... dating it is not enough at day granularity') applies verbatim to this fraction.
findings.failure_scenario: The next reader re-measures, gets a different fraction, and treats the paragraph specifically written to survive re-measurement as stale -- the failure the sentence above it was redrafted three times to avoid. Fix: 'many verdict files carry no task at all (M4.29), so their rounds count against nothing', with no fraction, or quote it as a floor the way the 22 is.

findings.summary: The row replaces one unanchored line offset with another, in the sentence that denounces line offsets. 'A draft said "fourteen lines below", which was the distance in HEAD; this commit rewrites that region and it is now 52.' In the staged file the new rounds: read is line 143 and the older worktree read spans `p = 'baselines/review.txt'` (194), `if os.path.exists(p):` (195) and `for line in open(p):` (196), so the distance is 51, 52 or 53 depending on an anchor the sentence never states. M4.31 -- filed by this same commit -- will rewrite exactly this region, and this round deleted the equivalent distance from M4.30 for this reason.
findings.failure_scenario: Whoever implements M4.26 counts 52 lines into a file that has since moved, lands on the wrong line, and re-learns that the offset was never anchored -- while the remedy the same row uses elsewhere was available. Fix: name the block ('the per-role `unresolved` python heredoc') instead of its distance.
